title: Swing Basics
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/0/title: Swing trading means catching a wave
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/0/body: **Swing trading** means catching one **wave** of a price move and holding the position for **a few days to a few weeks**. Swing traders mostly work on the **4-hour and daily** charts and take only a handful of trades a month.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/0/visual/symbo: One wave on the daily chart
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/1/body: Swing trading needs **less screen time**, and since targets are bigger, the **spread** eats only a small slice of your profit. On the flip side, positions stay open overnight and over the weekend, so you face **swap** fees and **gap risk**, and a wider stop means a **smaller position**.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/1/example/resu: Cost as a share of target
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/2/prompt: This swing trade is on the daily chart. How many pips is the take profit from the entry?
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/2/explanation: 1.0980 − 1.0820 = 0.0160, which is 160 pips. Swing targets are usually tens to hundreds of pips, much bigger than in scalping or day trading.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/3/prompt: How long does a swing trader usually hold a position?
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/3/options/0: A few days to a few weeks
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/3/options/1: A few seconds to a few minutes
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/3/options/2: Only until the end of the day
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/3/explanation: Swing trading means catching a full wave on the daily or 4-hour chart, which usually takes a few days to a few weeks.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/4/statement: A swing trader has to watch the charts all day so they don't miss any move.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/4/explanation: Swing traders make decisions on 4-hour and daily candles and work with pending orders and stop losses. Checking in a few times a day is plenty.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/5/prompt: Maryam has an office job and half an hour free every evening. Why does swing trading suit her better than day trading?
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/5/options/0: Analysis on daily candles and preset orders don't need her there all the time
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/5/options/1: Swing trading has no risk at all
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/5/options/2: Swing trading always makes more money
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/5/options/3: Swing trading doesn't need a stop loss
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/5/explanation: The real benefit of swing trading for Maryam is the schedule, not guaranteed profit or zero risk. Swing trades still have risk and stop losses. She just doesn't need to be at the charts in the middle of the day.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/6/pairs/0/mean: One wave from low to high, or the reverse
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/6/pairs/1/mean: A temporary move against the trend
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/6/pairs/2/mean: Price jumping while the market is closed
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/6/pairs/3/mean: An order that triggers at a set price
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/7/sentence: Swing traders usually work on the ___ and daily timeframes and hold positions for a few ___.
lessons/swing-u1-l1/steps/7/explanation: The 4-hour and daily timeframes show multi-day waves. The 1-minute timeframe and holding for a few seconds belong to scalping.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/0/body: Swing traders analyze **top-down**: they find the trend and key levels on the **weekly or daily**, then look for a setup and entry on the **4-hour**. Many keep the two timeframes about **4 to 6 times** apart.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/1/body: When the daily trend is **up**, a drop on the 4-hour usually counts as a **pullback** within that trend, not the start of a downtrend, as long as the last key low hasn't broken. Those pullbacks are exactly what swing traders watch for buys.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/1/tip: Many swing traders only check the chart after a 4-hour or daily candle closes.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/2/prompt: Put a swing trader's top-down analysis in order.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/2/items/1: Mark key levels on the daily
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/2/items/2: Look for a setup on the 4-hour
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/2/items/3: Set your order and stop loss
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/2/explanation: Each higher timeframe gives context to the one below it. The entry is the last step, and it only makes sense when it lines up with the higher-timeframe trend and levels.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/3/prompt: The daily trend is up, and this is the 4-hour chart. What's price doing right now?
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/3/options/0/la: Pulling back within the bigger trend
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/3/explanation: After a rally with higher highs and higher lows, a few small red candles showed up, and they haven't broken the last key low yet. In a daily uptrend, that's a pullback, exactly where a swing trader looks to buy.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/4/prompt: Which timeframe combo is most common for swing trading?
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/4/options/0: Daily for the trend, 4-hour for the entry
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/4/options/1: 1-minute for the trend, 5-second for the entry
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/4/options/2: 4-hour for the trend, daily for the entry
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/4/options/3: 15-minute for the trend, 1-minute for the entry
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/4/explanation: The trend comes from the higher timeframe and the entry from the lower one. The third option is backwards, and the others belong to scalping and day trading.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/5/statement: For a swing trader, the trend direction on the daily chart matters more than the swings on the 1-minute timeframe.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/5/explanation: 1-minute moves are just noise for a multi-day trade. The main swing decisions are made on the daily and 4-hour.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/6/prompt: The daily trend is up. On the 4-hour, price broke resistance at 1.0900, came back to it and printed a bullish engulfing. What do you do?
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/6/explanation: The old resistance turned into support after the break, and the bullish engulfing on that level shows buyers defended it. With the daily trend up, more upside is likely. Stop loss goes below the pullback low.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/7/sentence: A swing trader finds the trend on the ___ timeframe and the entry on the ___ timeframe.
lessons/swing-u1-l2/steps/7/explanation: The higher timeframe tells you the overall direction, and the lower timeframe gives you more precise entry timing and a tighter stop.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/0/body: A **swing high** is a candle whose high is above the highs of the few candles **before and after it** (say, 2 on each side). A **swing low** is the opposite: its low is below the candles on both sides. These are the points where the move changed direction.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/1/body: If each high is above the last (**HH**) and each low is above the last too (**HL**), the trend is up. **LH** and **LL** mean a downtrend. In an uptrend, a break of the **last HL** is the first warning that the trend is weakening.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/2/prompt: What kind of swing is the point marked with a ?
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/2/explanation: This point is a swing low (the candles on both sides have higher lows), and it's above the previous low (the last HL), so it's an HL. The uptrend is still healthy.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/3/prompt: Tap the last swing low (HL) in this uptrend.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/3/explanation: This candle's low is below the two candles before it and the two after it, so it's a swing low. It's also above the previous swing low, so it's an HL. No new swing low has formed since.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/4/prompt: The lows of five candles in a row are: 1.0850, 1.0838, 1.0822, 1.0835, 1.0846. Which candle is the swing low?
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/4/explanation: The third candle's low is below the two candles before it (1.0850 and 1.0838) and the two after it (1.0835 and 1.0846). That's the definition of a swing low with 2 candles on each side.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/5/statement: In a healthy uptrend, each swing low is higher than the previous swing low.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/5/explanation: Higher lows (HL) mean buyers are stepping in earlier each time. If a low forms below the previous one, the bullish structure is in question.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/6/prompt: The trend is climbing with HH and HL. Price pulled back, stayed above the last HL, and the last candle is a hammer. What's the swing trader's next step?
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/6/explanation: The pullback stopped above the last HL, and the hammer shows buyers are back, so a new HL is probably forming. Buying with the trend, with a stop below the hammer's low, has better odds of working.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/7/prompt: Put the steps for reading the trend with swings in order.
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/7/items/0: Mark the swing highs and lows
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/7/items/1: Compare each high and low with the previous one
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/7/items/2: Call the trend from HH/HL or LH/LL
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/7/items/3: Note the last swing for your stop loss
lessons/swing-u1-l3/steps/7/explanation: First the points, then the comparison, then the conclusion about the trend. The last swing is the line that invalidates the idea if it breaks, so it's the natural spot for your stop.
